Unfortunately, all that success meant the sharks were circling, and Kennesaw State lost several key players to the transfer portal this offseason. Thus, it's no surprise that the Owls have sputtered to a 1-4 start in 2026. That said, they should have a decent chance to build some momentum against Missouri State on Wednesday night. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN from Robert W. Plaster Stadium in Springfield, Missouri. Both squads enter Week 7 sitting at 1-4 and stinging from recent defeats. The Bears are regrouping after a decisive 34-13 road loss to Western Kentucky, while the Owls hope to rebound from a heartbreaking 27-26 defeat at the hands of Jacksonville State. My Kennesaw State vs Missouri State prediction weighs the rushing matchup against two offenses looking for a more complete performance. The win prices and a separate total pick follow. The Owls average 376.4 total yards per game with a rushing attack churning out 157.0 yards at a healthy 4.73 per carry. Missouri State is the wrong opponent for that. The Bears surrender 449.6 total yards and 32.4 points per game, and they get gashed on the ground specifically, allowing 196.4 rushing yards at 4.77 per carry. Rickie Collins is the engine for Kennesaw State. He has passed for 1,042 yards while adding 246 rushing yards and four touchdowns, giving the Owls a quarterback who can extend drives with his legs when the pocket breaks down. He has help behind him too. Boogie Woods III and Latrelle Murrell combine to average 5.2 yards a carry, which is exactly the profile you want against a front allowing almost 200 rushing yards per game. Kennesaw State has scored just 22.6 points per game, but its last two losses came by one and three points. Against this defense, I like the Owls to turn another competitive game into a win. picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Still, he's the driving force behind this offense considering he also leads the way in a quarterback-centric rushing attack. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 4 Ohio State is looking for revenge against No. 5 Indiana after last year's Big Ten title game Getty Images The 100th all-time meeting between Ohio State and Indiana should be a good one. The No. 5 Hoosiers host the fourth-ranked Buckeys with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to Indianapolis. The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss). Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith , who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category. This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State. Ohio State vs. Indiana: Need to know Annual top-five matchup: For the first 97 meetings between these teams, there were zero top-five matchups. When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands. Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year. Sacking Sayin: One way to make sure Smith never gets the football is to hit Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin while he still has the ball. That's exactly what the Hoosiers did in the Big Ten title game, sacking Sayin five times. Indiana has the personnel to get after Sayin again this time around. Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Memorial Stadium -- Bloomington, Indiana TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. Ohio State hits enough big plays with Smith to create some breathing room late. Can the Hoosiers take down the Buckeyes ? If so, they’ll need most of these predictions to come to fruition. 3 bold predictions for Indiana vs. Ohio State Maryland Terrapins linebacker Daniel Wingate (1) hits Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) during the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium in Columbus on Oct. 10, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times Indiana sacks Julian Sayin five times In the 2025 regular season, Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin was sacked six total times in 12 games. Indiana’s defense got to him five times in the Big Ten Championship Game alone. This 2026 matchup should be more of the same – if not an even more dominant showing from the Hoosiers’ pass-rushing attack. Halfway through the regular season, Sayin has already been sacked 11 times. And Indiana has a whopping 20 sacks in six games. The writing is on the wall – in Sharpie. Expect the Hoosiers to apply a lot of pressure on Sayin. It’ll be interesting to see how Sayin responds, especially considering he’s shown off his legs more often this year (and Indiana has been vulnerable to QBs who take off). In the 2025 conference title game, these two teams combined for 23 points in an old-fashioned, rugged Big Ten slugfest. But this Ohio State offense is operating at a different level. It has put up at least 31 points in every league game thus far. Sayin and stud wide receiver Jeremiah Smith have been flat-out unstoppable. As for the Hoosiers, they have scored at least 20 in every outing in 2026. Then again, Indiana scored six points through three quarters last Saturday at Nebraska. And, on the flip side, Ohio State hasn’t seen a defense half as sturdy as Indiana’s, aside from Texas, which held the Buckeyes to only three points in the second half. If Indiana’s defense strings together four full quarters, it can bottle up this Ohio State offense – or at least keep it at bay (Smith won’t be entirely shut down by any defense this year). And the expectation is that the Hoosiers offense, which has sputtered at times this year, struggles with this Buckeyes defense. It’d be a surprise to see either team score three touchdowns. Indiana, which is holding opponents to a Big Ten best 75.0 rushing yards per game, has been an absolute brick wall against the run. Ohio State, meanwhile, hasn’t exactly been running through anybody. It managed just 94 rushing yards against Texas in Week 2. Kent State held the Buckeyes to 3.8 yards per carry. You get the idea. In general, Ohio State’s experienced offensive line has been surprisingly uninspiring in 2026. Expect Indiana’s elite defensive front to have its way getting after Sayin and stifling the run game. But can the Hoosiers do enough against Smith? That will be the question. My Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction is riding with the home underdog as Bloomington takes center stage for a historic showdown. Saturday's noon ET clash on FOX's Big Noon Saturday marks Memorial Stadium's first-ever top-five matchup, and the Hoosiers are looking to make it one to remember. The Buckeyes arrive in Bloomington as 3.5-point favorites, but the Hoosiers have matchup advantages and Curt Cignetti's track record on their side. Find more college football picks for Saturday's slate. TOP PICK Who will win Ohio State vs Indiana: Indiana +3.5 I'm locking in a trade on the Indiana Hoosiers at +3.5 over the Ohio State Buckeyes and would play them down to a pick'em. Indiana has a strength-on-weakness edge over Ohio State in pass protection, and the Hoosiers have better standard-down success and line-yards-per-snap differentials , per GameOnPaper.com . Meanwhile, Indiana's defense can make the Buckeyes one-dimensional on offense. The Hoosiers rank sixth in the country in defensive rushing success rate, and Ohio State is only 81st in yards per rush. I also trust Curt Cignetti more in this spot. He's 6-2 straight up and 5-3 against the spread vs. top-10 opponents at Indiana , with a +13.8 spread differential. The Hoosiers beat Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten title game, and now get the Buckeyes at home with points. Ohio State vs Indiana Over/Under pick: Over 49.5 I'd play the Over at any total below 51.5 . The Hoosiers are 15-8 to the Over in Big Ten play under Cignetti, and this is a matchup between the two best quarterbacks in the Big Ten. Indiana's Josh Hoover and Ohio State's Julian Sayin rank first and second in the Big Ten in passer efficiency , and both have elite outside weapons. Sayin is throwing to the best wide receiver in the country, Jeremiah Smith, while Hoover has wideouts Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, who rank 14th and 15th nationally out of 1,004 qualifiers in PFF's wide receiver grade . According to GameOnPaper.com , both teams rank in the 90th percentile or higher in offensive explosive play rate . An early Buckeyes lead would force Indiana to open things up, which should create the kind of shootout this combo needs. The key is Indiana responding instead of letting Ohio State create separation. If Cignetti makes the better second-half adjustments, like he usually does, the Hoosiers can erase an early deficit, keep the score climbing, and stay within a field goal in the process. Collin Wilson Sat, October 17, 2026 at 9:33 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ohio State Buckeyes take on the Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington, Indiana, on Saturday, Oct. 17. Kickoff is set for 12 p.m. ET on FOX. Ohio State is favored by -3.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -182. Indiana, meanwhile, enters as a +3.5 underdog and is +150 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 50.5 total points. Here's my Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 17. Ohio State vs. Indiana Pick: Indiana +3.5 · Under 51 My Indiana vs. Ohio State best bet is on the Hoosiers to cover as short home underdogs and for the game to stay under the total. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Ohio State vs Indiana Odds Ohio State vs Indiana Spread : Ohio State -3.5 (-110), Indiana +3.5 (-110) Ohio State vs Indiana Over/Under : 50.5 (-110o / -110u) Ohio State vs Indiana Moneyline : Ohio State -182, Indiana +150 Revenge is on Ohio State 's mind after losing the Big Ten Championship to Indiana last season. Head coach Ryan Day had plenty of success overseeing the offensive play-calling, creating five pass explosives with quarterback Julian Sayin under center. The Buckeyes generated over 250 yards of passing in the championship game, with 10 targets and 144 yards going to Heisman hopeful Jeremiah Smith . The more surprising number is the final score. Smith ran wild in the passing game, but Ohio State managed to score just 10 points. While the offense looks to an explosive passing attack, the defense has been one of the best in FBS against the pass. Coordinator Matt Patricia's 3-3-5 defense ranks top-15 in Success Rate against the pass while grading second overall in coverage, per PFF . Cover 1 and Cover 3 have been the go-to looks for the Ohio State defense, preventing explosives at a top-20 rate in standard downs. However, there have been leaks when it comes to rush defense, with a rank outside the top 50 in Success Rate. The Buckeyes have been fantastic against zone read, but teams that use man blocking assignments have controlled the line of scrimmage . Ohio State ranks 60th in Line Yards, producing a low 25% Success Rate when opponents use man-blocking run concepts. Although Indiana 's turnover margin sits at +3 on the season, the Hoosiers have had no luck with loose balls. Head coach Curt Cignetti's defense has seen nine opponent fumbles through six games without a single recovery . Despite a low turnover margin in favor of Indiana, the defense has been lights-out against the rush. The Hoosiers rank fifth in Rushing Success Rate allowed and seventh in Defensive Line Yards, stopping opponents with inside zone at a 71% clip. Indiana has also dominated counter, a key run concept that complements inside zone. Defensive coordinator Bryant Haines has a defense that's second-best in FBS at shutting opponents down on standard downs. A big part of that is the fact that the Hoosiers have the third-most tackles for loss, led by EDGE Tobi Osunsanmi. Offensively, the rushing attack has taken a step back from Indiana's 2025 production, as Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard spearhead a Success Rate just outside the top 50. The offensive line has done its part in clearing holes, ranking top-25 in both Line Yards and Stuff Rate. Richard has been the spark plug for a rush attack that's 35th in EPA, averaging 4.9 yards after first contact. Despite 27 fewer rushing attempts, Richard has forced 31 missed tackles compared to Beebe's 22. The transition from Fernando Mendoza to Josh Hoover has seen little drop-off for the Indiana passing attack, as the TCU transfer has no interceptions and just a single turnover-worthy play on the season . Wide receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh have been electric, each racking up 41 targets and at least 3.7 yards per route run. The first handicap is how Indiana's defense will handle the threat of Smith on every snap Ohio State plays. Smith provided eight catches and explosives in the Big Ten Championship, but a collective effort in the second level kept the receiver from the end zone. The only touchdown from the Buckeyes was scored by Carnell Tate, who has since moved on to the NFL. The biggest issue in OSU's passing game is the lack of a second option for Sayin. Devin McCuin ranks second in targets, but his 21 targets are dwarfed by Smith's 66. Expect Indiana to limit every player on the field not named Smith while minimizing assignment errors and missed tackles. The game plan worked in last year's Big Ten Championship, but with Smith involved in a heavier amount of motion, the Hoosiers have their work cut out for them in Week 7. On the ground, Ohio State's rushing attack may have issues getting jump-started against Indiana. The Buckeyes utilize both inside and outside zone at a high Success Rate with Bo Jackson. The sophomore averages 3.9 yards after first contact, but Indiana has dominated inside zone this season. Any success in the running game will come outside the tackle box with no expectation of explosives, as Indiana has allowed just two opponent rushing attempts to exceed 20 yards . The path to success is much clearer for Indiana's run game, as its secondary run concept of man-blocking assignments is a large weakness for Ohio State. That leads to Richard, who has a near even split of zone-read and man-blocking rushing attempts. The Buckeyes rank 62nd in Rush EPA allowed, so Richard should be the driving force behind moving the chains to create methodical drives. A grind of a game is expected, and Indiana should have the better rushing offense in the final box score. The Hoosiers' key is limiting explosives on defense and limiting breakaway scores for Smith. The biggest gap in the game is Ohio State's limited receiving unit, as Sayin has been hesitant to target any option other than Smith. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings call for Ohio State to be favored by -1.5, giving Indiana the edge in the current market. Pick: Indiana +3.5 · Under 51

Manning's inconsistency has kept the Longhorns' offense largely out of rhythm this season, a critique he'll try to correct against the SEC's worst defense. After a loss to rival Oklahoma sent the Longhorns falling six spots in the AP Poll, Texas is hoping to use the tailspinning Gators as their punching bag to stay in the College Football Playoff picture. Florida has lost back-to-back SEC games in blowout fashion , tumbling out of the national rankings without a clear solution to stop the hemorrhaging. Sumrall said progress is sometimes "dysfunctional" and agreed with some of the booing he experienced on the sideline of last week's loss to South Carolina . Simmons collected five sacks during a win at Tennessee last month and is the runaway favorite to win the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year honor. Texas vs. Florida: Need to know Turnovers and touchdowns: Manning's production against Power Four competition has been pedestrian -- four touchdown passes and four interceptions. Two came during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six that swung the game's momentum to the Sooners. Manning's been sacked 12 times through five games -- 10 coming against Ohio State , Tennessee and Oklahoma. If there's a get-right opportunity for Florida's defense, perhaps this is it. Frightening defensive numbers: Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense, explosive plays allowed, pass defense and 15th in scoring defense this season. Sumrall said this week he was taking a closer look at multiple areas of his team to try and fix what has nuked this 4-0 start for the Gators. It starts with getting stops on defense against the Longhorns. Who will win Florida vs Texas: Texas -10.5 Have the Florida Gators been "figured out"? I'm not sure. Expect the Longhorns to win with long, methodical drives that drain the clock rather than quick-strike scores. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A Friday cold front drops the temperatures near 50 degrees at kickoff and won't rise much above 70. There may be a few clouds but not much chance of rain. Texas vs Florida football betting info Moneyline: Texas -205, Florida +195 Spread: Texas is favored by 10½ points. Over/under : 52½ Texas history: Florida All-time: Texas leads 3-1-1 Last meeting: Florida 29, Texas 21 (Oct. 4, 2025) Most memorable meeting : Texas 7, Florida 7 (1924). A reported crowd of approximately 10,000 fans filled Clark Field, the current location of the Caven Lacrosse and Sports Center across San Jacinto Boulevard from Royal-Memorial Stadium. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. He's been active with 15 total tackles and three tackles for a loss but doesn't play at the level of the linemen from Oklahoma, Ohio State or Tennessee. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. I doubt the offense will have solved all of its problems over the past week, and don't get me started on the special teams. But only minimal improvement from Arch's bunch will be necessary if the Longhorns continue to play well against the run and subdue Jadan Baugh. Cedric Golden: Texas 27, Florida 20. The Horns respond in favorable fashion but questions remain about this offense and its inability to run the ball. Michael Shapiro: Texas 35, Florida 20. The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Two losses for Texas at this point in the season would make things very uncomfortable in Austin, and perhaps it would mark the beginning of the end for some important names there. I don't think that's going to happen, though. I think Texas bounces back this week behind a strong defensive performance and looks the part against Florida. If the Longhorns can limit Jaden Baugh, they'll defend home field without much issue. I think Florida hangs around, but the Longhorns put it away in the fourth quarter. – Brandon Little , A to Z Ohio State Final Prediction for Florida vs. Texas It shouldn't be much of a surprise that none of our experts have picked the Gators, as they have lost our trust after the disastrous performances of the last two weeks. A win here would do wonders to get them back in our good graces. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Florida vs Texas Odds Florida vs Texas Spread : Texas -10.5 (-112), Florida +10.5 (-108) Florida vs Texas Over/Under : 52.5 (-110o / -110u) Florida vs Texas Moneyline : Florida +330, Texas -425 It has been a very up-and-down campaign for the Gators in former Tulane head coach Jon Sumrall's first season in Gainesville after leading the Green Wave to the College Football Playoff last season. Florida prevailed in its first four games under Sumrall, notably taking out Auburn on the road, followed by a dominant blowout victory over then-top-five Ole Miss by a whopping 24-point margin. Now, the Gators have dropped consecutive games to Missouri and South Carolina and must head on the road to Austin to face a Longhorn bunch that will also be highly motivated after a disappointing Week 6 loss to rival Oklahoma. Despite Florida's back-to-back losses, quarterback Aaron Philo has largely impressed in his first season in Gainesville after spending his first two years at Georgia Tech . Philo's 1,341 passing yards heading into Week 7 rank 40th in college football, with the former Yellow Jacket also ranking 33rd with a QBR of 74.1. The Gators also boast an elite rushing attack led by running back Jadan Baugh, whose 12 rushing touchdowns lead all of college football after the first six weeks of action. Florida's offense sits 12th in the nation in points scored, averaging a whopping 41.7 points per game over its first six games despite scoring just 36 points over its last two contests. While there's no doubt what Sumrall's offense is capable of offensively, the defense has glaring holes that were on full display against LaNorris Sellers and South Carolina. In fact, the Gamecocks scored nearly 40 points on Florida's defense on the road. The Gators have allowed their opponents to score nearly 30 PPG on the season thus far, which should definitely be problematic against an Arch Manning -led Texas offense that will undoubtedly give this defense its toughest challenge of the season. Despite dropping its first game of the season in devastating fashion on Saturday, the Longhorns are still receiving sizable respect in betting markets. Texas currently stands as a double-digit favorite to take down Florida in Week 7. Texas quarterback Arch Manning entered his final season in Austin as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites but has been quite inconsistent over the Longhorns' first six games. While the senior has thrown for 1,122 passing yards and 10 touchdowns, Manning has been very susceptible to turning the ball over, already throwing five interceptions thus far. Arch also hasn't been quite as dominant as he had been rushing the football in previous seasons. He has yet to record a touchdown with his legs despite his dual-threat ability being a key to his game. Although Manning has had an up-and-down 2026 campaign, the Longhorns' offensive unit has still thrived for the most part due to it boasting versatile playmakers all over the field. Auburn transfer wide receiver Cam Coleman leads an impressive Texas receiving corps with 318 yards and five touchdowns, and the WR room also has stars in Ryan Wingo and Emmett Mosley V. Former NC State running back Hollywood Smothers paces an elite Longhorn rushing attack with 237 yards to go with two rushing touchdowns. He plays alongside Arizona State transfer Raleek Brown, who has recorded four of Texas' six rushing touchdowns this season. The Longhorns are even better on the other side of the ball after adding defensive coordinator Will Muschamp. Texas' defense has allowed opponents to score just 16 points per game on the season thus far, ranking 21st in the nation. The front seven has been remarkably impressive over the first six games of the season, with EDGE Colin Simmons leading the nation with 9.5 sacks. The Horns' 18 total sacks also rank inside the top 10 in the country. Texas has allowed opposing offenses less than 265 yards of total offense per game and boasts an elite red-zone touchdown rate of just 33%, which is tied for second nationally. While the Longhorns undoubtedly have one of the top defenses in all of college football, it has forced just five turnovers in six games, which is certainly an area for improvement heading into a loaded SEC schedule. Florida and Texas will duke it out on Saturday afternoon in what definitely sets up to be one of the best matchups on the Week 7 slate. While the Gators boast an unbelievably impressive offense that Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian won't take lightly, their loss to South Carolina revealed some holes. From a betting perspective, I like backing the Longhorns to cover the -6.5 first-half spread in what I expect to be a very quick start for a highly motivated Texas squad. This Texas defense will be far and away Florida's toughest challenge to date, and I'm inclined to back Sarkisian's bunch to get off to a red-hot start over the game's first 30 minutes. Pick: Texas 1H -6.5

Here's what you need to know heading into the matchup as The Big Lead locks in our final prediction for this Week 7 college football clash. Texas offensive inconsistency and defensive strength Arch Manning has shown flashes but has been uneven against better competition, with turnovers becoming a recurring issue. The unit ranks among the better groups nationally in yards allowed and has been especially effective limiting yards after contact. The two-game skid has confirmed those worries. Missed tackles and coverage breakdowns have piled up? The total damage? Florida is the SEC's worst defense in total output, explosive plays allowed, and against the pass. It's the second-worst in scoring. On offense, the Florida run game that once looked dominant has been largely shut down by better fronts. Jadan Baugh's production has dropped sharply. After rushing for over 130 yards in four wins, his totals fell to 13 and then 59 yards in two losses. Questions also linger about quarterback availability with Aaron Philo listed as questionable. A potential shift to Tramell Jones Jr. would add even more uncertainty against a Texas defense that flies to the ball. Key matchup dynamics to watch Texas holds clear edges in defensive structure and home-field stability. Florida's ability to create explosive plays through play-action and yards after catch remains a theoretical strength, but recent film shows those opportunities drying up against disciplined units. Scheme-wise, Texas' ability to limit perimeter runs and finish tackles aligns poorly with what Florida has relied on. Manning should face less pressure than he did against Oklahoma, giving him cleaner looks against a secondary that has been vulnerable. Florida vs. Texas prediction: Who wins and why? Texas is the more complete team right now, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Even with offensive questions, the Longhorns' ability to control the line of scrimmage and force Florida into obvious passing situations should decide the game. Florida has the talent to keep stretches competitive, but the recent defensive regression and limited run game make a full road upset unlikely. The Big Lead Prediction: Texas 31, Florida 17

Lebby ran Kiffin's offense at Ole Miss in 2020 and 2021, and the Rebels' 2020 attack set an SEC record for total offense in conference play. Kiffin called him "a huge part of our success there" this week. Now Mississippi State's head coach, he leads the Bulldogs into a top-25 showdown with LSU on Saturday. "I don't like playing against him because they go so fast," Kiffin said this week. LSU (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is reeling after an overtime loss at Kentucky last week, and finds itself in a familiar place under previous coaches: two losses at the midpoint of the season. It wasn't supposed to start this way for Kiffin, who took over a program with deep pockets and turned the roster over into one of the most talented in the country. A third conference loss in Kiffin's first season would leave almost no margin for November, with Alabama and Texas still coming to Baton Rouge. Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) has already won two SEC games, exceeding the one Lebby collected in his first two seasons combined. Alabama rode into Starkville and won 56-23 two weeks ago, and Kamario Taylor , the sophomore quarterback who spent September in the Heisman Trophy conversation, finished the day on the sideline with a boot on his right foot. Two weeks later, nobody outside the Bulldogs' building knows if he will play. Lebby said the SEC availability report would answer that question. LSU vs. Mississippi State: Need to know Kamario Taylor's right foot : Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards and an SEC-best 17 touchdowns with four interceptions. He's thrown three touchdowns in the last five games, the longest stretch since LSU's Jayden Daniels in 2023. He first hurt his foot in the win over Missouri , and it showed against the Tide. He was sacked five times and finished with minus-26 rushing yards before leaving the game. If he can't play, Lebby's options are redshirt freshman Parker Puckett and AJ Swann , who spent a season at LSU. Where is Mississippi State's ground game? Fluff Bothwell has 403 yards and three touchdowns on 74 carries, but he had only one carry against Alabama and spent most of the afternoon with a boot on his left foot. The Bulldogs were outrushed 179-18. Now they get a defense that ranked second nationally against the run through four weeks, allowing 47.5 yards per game. Kentucky found cracks last week. CJ Baxter broke a 77-yard run on the first snap and finished with 123 yards. The Wildcats ran for 155 yards. The Sam Leavitt Experience : LSU QB Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,496 yards and 10 touchdowns, but he has thrown an interception in every game this season, totaling eight through six games. No one in the FBS has thrown more interceptions. At Kentucky, he completed 25 of 34 passes for 275 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another in overtime, but he also threw a pick and lost a fumble on a sack in the fourth quarter. LSU's recent success : The Tigers have won the last three meetings against Mississippi State. The Bulldogs last won in Baton Rouge in 2020, when they pulled off a 44-34 upset in Mike Leach's first season. This is the first meeting since 2023. The teams used to play each other annually, but that ended when the SEC expanded to 16 teams in 2024. Strip away overtime, and LSU's three SEC games have produced 56, 41 and 54 combined points. Not one cleared 58.5. Kiffin's offense averages 42 points per game, but against SEC defenses LSU has scored 24, 35 and 27 in regulation. Mississippi State scores 39 points per game, but that production was built on Taylor's legs and Bothwell's workload. Both are in question against a front that has been among the nation's best against the run. Mississippi State's SEC games have averaged nearly 70 total points, and if Taylor is close to 100%, Lebby's tempo can drag LSU into a bayou shootout. It's hard to bet on that version of Taylor showing up two weeks after he left Alabama in a boot. LSU heads into the matchup with a recent loss, while the Bulldogs are also traveling to Baton Rouge after a loss to the Crimson Tide in Week 5. Before the No. 22 LSU Tigers host the No. 16 Mississippi State Bulldogs this Saturday, the LSU On SI team predicts which team will win and why. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ross Abboud The time for sloppiness is over, and everyone in LSU’s football program knows it. Ole Miss was a game you could’ve won. Kentucky was a game you should never have lost. That will be LSU’s wake-up call. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. If both Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell miss or are limited by their injuries, I expect LSU’s defense to be too much for Mississippi State to handle. I think the Tigers come out with a point to prove and get to work proving it. LSU 31, Mississippi State 14 Hannah Garcia While there’s the possibility of Taylor and Bothwell being out for the game, the LSU defense is still missing key pieces in Spears and Whit Weeks. The receivers have struggled to find consistency all season with catching the ball and Sam Leavitt’s interception numbers are also something that I think could cause LSU to lose. Mississippi State 24, LSU 17 LSU is desperate to bounce back after a tough loss against Kentucky. The keys to this game are Kamario Taylor’s health and Mississippi State’s secondary. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. Meanwhile, the Bulldogs allow the second-most passing yards per game in the SEC, so I expect Lane Kiffin to open up the playbook and attack that weakness. I think the Tigers handle business at home. QB Kamario Taylor is officially questionable with a foot injury , and his availability could completely change the outlook of this matchup. Taylor has been outstanding through five games, completing 66.2% of his passes for 1,450 yards and 17 touchdowns against only four interceptions, while adding another 159 yards and a score on the ground. He's been the engine behind an offense generating +0.22 EPA/Play with a 48.7% success rate, but those numbers become considerably less meaningful if Taylor isn't under center. Taylor initially suffered the injury against Missouri before aggravating it during Mississippi State's 56-23 loss to Alabama, when he was visibly hobbled and eventually exited in the fourth quarter. He was later spotted wearing a protective boot on his right foot. Even if Taylor is cleared to play Saturday, there's a significant difference between being healthy enough to take snaps and being capable of operating Jeff Lebby's offense at full capacity. His mobility is an important component of Mississippi State's offensive identity, and limiting his ability to escape pressure or extend plays could be devastating against an LSU defense that ranks first nationally in EPA/Play allowed. If Taylor can't go, Billy Puckett or AJ Swann would be tasked with replacing one of the SEC's most productive quarterbacks in one of college football's most hostile road environments. That's a massive downgrade, obviously, and it's going to create a massive disadvantage for the Bulldogs' offense. The Bulldogs are also dealing with uncertainty surrounding RB Fluff Bothwell, who's questionable with an ankle injury after leaving the Alabama game early. Bothwell leads Mississippi State with 403 rushing yards and three touchdowns, meaning the Bulldogs could be without both their starting quarterback and leading rusher. That's not exactly ideal when you're heading into Death Valley. LSU is coming off a brutal 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, and while I'm not particularly interested in blindly betting on a team because it's supposedly angry, this is a matchup where the Tigers should have significant advantages on both sides of the football. The defensive profile is the biggest reason I'm willing to lay the lumber. LSU is allowing -0.24 EPA/Play, ranking first nationally, and has consistently prevented opposing offenses from sustaining drives. That's particularly important against a Mississippi State offense whose efficiency has been driven largely by Taylor's ability to create explosives through the air and extend plays with his legs. If Taylor is limited, LSU should have considerably more opportunities to generate havoc without sacrificing coverage downfield. The offensive matchup is also juicy, making it a great bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin's team. LSU is averaging 42 points and 524.8 yards per game, including 311 passing yards per contest, while Mississippi State's defense ranks 92nd nationally in EPA/Play allowed. The Bulldogs are also allowing 260 passing yards per game (124th) and just surrendered 56 points to Alabama. That's a defense I'm particularly interested in going up against Lane Kiffin's offense, as there should be ample opportunity for the Tigers to score early and often. Mississippi State will also be without LB Jalen Smith, its second-leading tackler, while LB Zakari Tillman is doubtful. Those absences could create additional problems for a defense that already struggles to consistently get off the field. I'm willing to lay LSU -12.5, and the uncertainty surrounding Taylor is a significant reason why. This number opened around LSU -11.5 before getting bet toward two touchdowns, and I'm much more interested in laying the Tigers below 14 than chasing the move afterward. Mississippi State's offense ranks 25th nationally in EPA/Play, but that efficiency has been built around Taylor's production. We're talking about a quarterback responsible for 18 total touchdowns who's now dealing with a foot injury serious enough to leave his status for Saturday uncertain. Even if he plays, I have serious questions about how effectively he'll be able to operate against an LSU defense allowing -0.24 EPA/Play. If he doesn't, the Bulldogs could be forced to start Puckett or Swann against one of the most efficient defenses in college football. Then there's Bothwell, whose questionable status creates another potential problem for an offense that needs balance to prevent LSU from consistently generating pressure. On the other side, LSU's offense gets a Mississippi State defense ranked 92nd in EPA/Play allowed and 124th in passing yards allowed, with additional injuries at linebacker. That's a pretty significant mismatch. I'm not going to pretend LSU's defense looked particularly impressive against Kentucky, but I'm willing to trust its season-long efficiency profile over one ugly performance. The Tigers should have the offensive advantage regardless of who starts for Mississippi State, and Taylor's injury creates a legitimate possibility that the Bulldogs struggle to keep pace. If Taylor is ruled out, I expect this number to become considerably less attractive. I'll lay it below two touchdowns. Pick: LSU -14

Can Lane Kiffin and the Tigers bounce back after an embarrassing loss? The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. How Each Team Wins For LSU, everything starts with protecting the football. Leavitt must avoid costly interceptions and take advantage of Mississippi State's vulnerable secondary. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. home.blurb: Whether the No. 22 Tigers will play good football when they host No. 16 Mississippi State on Saturday is to be determined, but LSU is undoubtedly beginning the second half of its season with some good fortune. With Bulldogs star quarterback Kamario Taylor and top rusher Fluff Bothwell both listed as doubtful on Friday night's SEC student-athlete availability report, the Tigers appear to have been handed a layup. Mississippi State's hobbled status gives the Tigers a great chance to start anew in the second half of the season after road losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky sullied the beginning of Kiffin's highly anticipated first season. While conventional wisdom suggests the Tigers need to win out and finish 10-2 to reach the CFP, there may still be some wiggle room. But the idea of the Tigers figuring things out in the season's second half isn't outlandish. Flashes of potency have been there, even during its losses. LSU averaged 5.8 yards per play against Kentucky and racked up 26 first downs. The Tigers also scored 17 unanswered on Ole Miss in the second half before faltering late. If LSU is going to squirm its way back into the College Football Playoff conversation following a 4-2 start and salvage an uninspired start to Lane Kiffin's coaching tenure, it's going to need good fortune and better football. Taking advantage of it will be critical for a Tigers team that still plays No. 6 Alabama , No. 7 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee . After opening as a 10.5-point favorite amid uncertainty over Taylor's status, the Tigers are now favored by 17. With Mississippi State's breakout star likely to be sidelined by a foot injury that he suffered in a Week 5 loss to Alabama, the Bulldogs have lost their bite. The expected absence of Bothwell will only make life harder on Mississippi State's offense as it potentially navigates life without Taylor, who ranks No. 5 nationally in total offense per game at 321.8 yards. If the Tigers finish 9-3, they will have an 84.9% chance of reaching the CFP, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. In that scenario, they would need to go 5-1 overall and 3-1 against the four teams remaining on their schedule who are currently ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Three of those four top-20 games are at home, including Saturday's tilt against Mississippi State. Such an outcome is squarely within the realm of possibility for an LSU team that flashed its high-end potential in dominant victories over the likes of Clemson and Texas A&M . Getting to 9-3 or 10-2 will require cleaner play on both sides of the football for LSU. Turnovers have been a recurring issue for the Tigers, who are tied for 117th with 10 giveaways. The defense has been inconsistent, allowing fewer than 200 yards in each of LSU's four wins and 400+ yards in the two losses. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. Pete Fiutak Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:26 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There are rivalries, and there's the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry that started in 1892 – only Minnesota vs Wisconsin has gone on longer than Auburn vs Georgia. No, it's not nearly as fierce as the Iron Bowl when Alabama takes on Auburn, but when you've played 130 times, you tend to have a few interesting moments that build into something generational. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. Auburn vs Georgia: Quick Hits Auburn gets LSU and the Lane Kiffin show next, and then goes to Ole Miss. Georgia gets a week off before playing the Cocktail Party showdown against Florida in Atlanta, and then it goes to Ole Miss. Georgia has won seven times in the series since losing in 2017 (it was No. 1 in the nation then, too), but it won the SEC Championship a few weeks later. The Bulldogs have won 11 of the last 12 meetings. How To Watch Auburn vs Georgia Date: Saturday, October 17, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Sanford Stadium, Athens, GA – CFN Week 7 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predictions For Every Remaining Game – CFN Week 7 Expert Picks Why Auburn Will Win The Auburn defense has been great. It might have been hit hard by Florida, but it does a lot of bending without breaking, thanks to plenty of sacks, lots of plays behind the line, and a third down defense that's holding up well. Offensively, the high-tempo Tiger attack should be able to keep the Bulldogs on their heels. Alabama ran well last week, but it only handed the ball off 29 times. Auburn won't make that mistake, pushing for at least 35 carries, and close to 40, as it tries to hit the Georgia defense with tempo. Why Georgia Will Win Georgia's defensive front will live in the Auburn backfield. It's a problem with Auburn's style that it allows defenses to tee off on the quarterback and come up with too many tackles for loss. The Tigers don't worry about the time of possession battle, and they're good at overcoming negative plays with something positive, but Georgia has the defense to swarm all over the quick-hitting short plays. Auburn doesn't do anything deep, and Georgia should limit any yards after the catch or runs that get to the second level. Auburn vs Georgia Prediction, Betting Lines It's been an interesting start to the Golesh era. The offense is supposed to dominate and take over, but it doesn't do it enough. The defense that was so great last year has stayed strong, but it's about to get pounded on. Auburn's two losses came when it allowed over three yards per carry. Georgia is averaging over six yards per pop. The Georgia Bulldogs are the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn is a team that's trying to turn their program around. And, Alex Golesh is looking for that first unranked-upset win over a rival. Can he get it done on Saturday? A to Z Sports' experts picked the final scores for this game. Final score predictions for Georgia vs. Auburn Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Georgia 30 Auburn 10 After watching the Georgia Bulldogs run all over the SEC's top-ranked rushing defense in Tuscaloosa, Auburn may be in trouble. Truthfully, Georgia is the best team in the country, and Auburn is rebuilding under first-year head coach Alex Golesh. I don't think this team has the explosiveness to score on Georgia, and they certainly don't have the physicality to win the trench battle on either side. Gunner Srockton has also elevated his game this season, making multiple high-leverage throws against Alabama in an extremely tough environment. The Dawgs will roll in this one. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Georgia 45, Auburn 17 I don't see this as much of a game. The Bulldogs are coming off a big win over the Alabama Crimson Tide and showed they can hang with the best in the business. This Auburn Tigers team is in good hands with Alex Golesh, but they aren't there yet. Byrum Brown won't be able to generate much against another great Bulldogs defense. This one will likely be over at halftime. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Georgia 38, Auburn 14 Georgia looks like the most complete team in the country right now, and I don't see Auburn keeping up for long in this matchup. The Bulldogs have the talent, physicality, and balance to control both sides of the ball, and I expect them to establish dominance early. Gunner Stockton is poised for a big game, taking advantage of Auburn's defense and helping Georgia put points on the board consistently. Once the Bulldogs find their offensive rhythm, the Tigers could struggle to keep this one competitive. The Georgia defense could be just as impressive. Auburn will likely have a few moments, but I don't expect the Tigers to sustain enough offense to seriously threaten the Bulldogs. Georgia can generate pressure, force mistakes, and turn defensive stops into scoring opportunities, letting the lead grow as the game progresses. This matchup highlights just how dangerous Georgia can be when all three phases click. The Bulldogs pull away comfortably and send another message to the country. Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Georgia 44, Auburn 20 Boy, we've kind of forgotten about Gunner Stockton in the big picture, haven't we? The Dawgs' starting quarterback has gotten lost in the shuffle this year, with strong quarterback play from Darian Mensah, Keelon Russell, Kamario Taylor, Josh Hoover, and others. But make no mistake, he executes his team's offense as well as any signal caller in the country, as we saw in Georgia's 20-17 win over Alabama last weekend. More of the same will come on Saturday against an Auburn team that will fight for a half and then find itself out of this by the third quarter. Stockton will continue to impress, running when he needs to and spreading the ball around at a high percentage (18/22 passing last week, with completions by 10 different pass catchers). Georgia might be banged up at RB, but Dwight Phillips Jr.'s 120 yards last week against Bama proved they're basically plug-and-play in the backfield. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Georgia 30, Auburn 10 The Georgia Bulldogs have now proven they are the No. 1 team in the country. away.headline: SEC Availability Report | Latest on Georgia's Nate Frazier, KJ Bolden for Auburn
away.blurb: Metro Phoenix Sports Things To Do Politics Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals BULLDOGS-EXTRA SEC Availability Report | Georgia's KJ Bolden downgraded to out for Auburn Marc Weiszer Athens Banner-Herald Oct. 14, 2026 Updated Oct. 16, 2026, 5:41 p.m. MT Georgia football 's third official availability report for Saturday's 3:30 p.m. home game against Auburn has been released by the SEC. Safety KJ Bolden, the star junior, is now listed as out. He was downgraded from questionable to doubtful on Wednesday. Wide receiver Isiah Canion and running back Chauncey Bowens are listed as out. Offensive lineman Marcus Harrison went from probable to not listed, meaning he's available to play. These Georgia players are listed as out These Georgia players are listed as doubtful These Georgia players are listed as questionable These Georgia players are listed as probable Auburn: OUT: Offensive lineman Tai Buster (undisclosed), TE Hunter Herring (undisclosed), LB Xavier Atkins (non-injury related). Georgia has six players listed on the latest report, updated most recently on Friday, Oct. 16. Bolden was helped to the sideline with an apparent leg injury after his third-down sack late in the win at Alabama but appeared Monday for his normal WSB interview. He was wearing a sleeve on the right leg during the interview. Bolden is fourth on the Bulldogs with 22 tackles and has one interception and two pass breakups. Running back Nate Frazier, who warmed up but did not play against Alabama due to a lingering rib injury, again is not on the availability report just like last week. Canion has missed the last three games with what coach Kirby Smart Monday called a "lower extremity injury." Bowens sustained a lower body injury in the win against Vanderbilt two weeks ago and did not play at Alabama. This is the third season that the conference has had reporting policies for schools ahead of SEC games. The SEC releases daily reports Wednesday, Thursday and Friday and another 90 minutes before kickoff on game day. This list will be updated in the days leading to kickoff. Running back Chauncey Bowens (lower body) Wide receiver Isiah Canion (leg). Outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee). Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (collarbone).

Safety KJ Bolden, the star junior, is now listed as out. He was downgraded from questionable to doubtful on Wednesday. Wide receiver Isiah Canion and running back Chauncey Bowens are listed as out. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Alabama looks to recover from its first loss of the season on Saturday at No. 14 Tennessee Getty Images A pair of historic rivals with playoff aspirations are squaring off in a top-15 SEC showdown on Saturday, as No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for the Third Saturday in October. The Crimson Tide will be looking to avoid losing consecutive regular season games for the first time since 2007, while the Volunteers will be seeking to snap a four-game home losing streak against ranked opponents. Alabama (5-1, 3-1 SEC) took a 20-17 home loss to Georgia last week, which leaves the Crimson Tide with a dwindling margin for error entering the second half of their schedule. Tennessee (5-1, 2-1) is coming off an ugly 24-17 win at Arkansas in need of the resume boost that would come with knocking off Alabama. While Tennessee's defense is thriving midway through the season, facing Alabama will be its toughest test yet. Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell leads the league in passing yards with 1,599 and brings game-changing mobility. Though Alabama star receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams is expected to miss the game due to injury, Bama's offense will still pack a punch that tests Tennessee's secondary. The Volunteers counter with the nation's No. 15 rushing offense and a languishing passing attack that will need to get better if they are going to pull an upset that would reverberate through the SEC and beyond. With blowout road wins over quality foes Kentucky and Mississippi State already in hand, the Tide will look to keep rolling on the road with their first win in Knoxville since 2020. Alabama vs. Tennessee: Need to know Neyland blues: The last time Tennessee beat a ranked team at Neyland Stadium was in 2024, when it edged No. 7 Alabama 24-17. The Vols finished 0-3 at home against ranked opponents last season and fell 20-17 to Texas in Week 4, extending their home losing streak against ranked opponents to four games. But something will have to give as the Crimson Tide have dropped two straight inside Neyland Stadium. Whichever team is smoking, the traditional postgame victory cigars will hit a little different this time. Tennessee's QB question: Tennessee sophomore quarterback George MacIntyre made his first career start last week in the Volunteers' 24-17 win at Arkansas, stepping in for injured and underperforming freshman Faizon Brandon . Now the question is how long the Volunteers will stick with MacIntyre, who completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions against the Razorbacks. Regardless of who gets the nod against Alabama, the Crimson Tide's priority will be to slow down the SEC's second-leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , and to make Tennessee's fledgling passing attack prove that it can deliver. Playoff implications: With a win, Alabama will have an 87.7% chance of reaching the College Football Playoff, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. A loss would drop that mark to 52.9% and crush Alabama's margin for error. Because the Crimson Tide's strength of schedule lags behind others in the SEC, its case for inclusion as a three-loss team would be shaky. Tennessee's playoff odds would shoot to 51.6% with a win and drop to 16.8% with a loss. Replicating that formula against Alabama won't be possible unless the Crimson Tide shoot themselves in the foot with turnovers and special team miscues. Because the Crimson Tide won't respect the Volunteers' passing game, they'll be able to load the box and frustrate Tennessee's ground game, much like Texas did in Week 4. Offensively, Alabama has too much firepower to be fully restrained for four quarters. Look for Bama to pull away in the fourth quarter. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas.
