Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 95+ yards. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! Russell has surpassed that mark in every game this season. Plus, the longest rush prop eliminates the possibility of sacks taking away rushing yards, so if you can access it, take it Over his standard rushing yards prop at 25+. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Essentially, Alabama proved they belong with the elite teams, with a resume boasting a win over the suddenly excellent Kentucky and a loss to #1 Georgia that could have gone either way. The Tennessee Volunteers are similarly 5-1, but it took squeaking out tight wins over SEC bottom feeders Arkansas and Auburn. The Vols have generally played well on defense, but their offense has left a LOT to be desired, with QB Faizon Brandon leading an anemic passing attack until he was injured, and backup George MacIntyre not doing any better. So they're sitting put with a #15 ranking. FanDuel's sportsbook has the opening odds set to Alabama holding a -6.5 favorite over Tennessee, with an over/under of 55.5. Week 1 – Beat Furman 56-9 Week 2 – Beat Georgia Tech 45-24 Week 3 – Beat Kennesaw State 42-9 Week 4 – Lost to Texas 17-20 Week 5 – Beat Auburn 24-14 Week 6 – Beat Arkansas 24-17 The Vols are averaging 22 points per game on offense and 17 points per game on defense in SEC play, with the biggest problem being that, for the season, they're averaging only 187 passing yards per game (and that includes their three warm up games to start the season). Running back DeSean Bishop is still carrying the entire offense with 678 rushing yards. Week 1 – Beat East Carolina 48-10 Week 2 – Beat Kentucky 45-17 Week 3 – Beat Florida State 50-36 Week 4 – Beat South Carolina 49-18 Week 5 – Beat Mississippi State 56-23 Week 6 – Lost to Georgia 17-20 The Tide's offense obliterated all of their first five foes, scoring 45+ in every single game despite having only a single cupcake game. Then Georgia happened, and the two elite squads turned the game into a low-possession, high-stakes contest (seriously, there were only 7 combined drives in the entire second half). The Alabama defense has had some struggles this year. They've been a playmaking defense, but they've also given up some downfield passes in almost every game, and then struggled with UGA's rushing attack last week. Still, the held the Dogs to less than half of their usual offensive output. Alabama boasts a much better offense, but the two teams have likely equivalent defenses. However, the game will be at Neyland Stadium. Still, the 6.5 spread with a 55.5 OU has the prediction something like a 31-25 Crimson Tide victory. How the Tide responds to a tough and disappointed loss in their clash with Georgia will be paramount, but I wouldn't be surprised if this one winds up going under the 55.5 points. Something more like a 21-14 kind of game. What do you think? Give us your thoughts in the comments below.

away.blurb: The Alabama Crimson Tide will look to bounce back after a razor close loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in Week 6 when they face off against the Tennessee Volunteers. But unfortunately, they will not be at full strength offensively in Saturday’s game. Junior wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams has been one of the more reliable and effective wide receivers in all of college football this season for the Crimson Tide. Prior to their loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams had put together a three-game streak of finding the end zone at least once. During their Week 6 loss to Georgia, Coleman-Williams was forced to exit the game after both seemingly re-aggravating a knee injury in the game and suffering a concussion, which was what ultimately cut his game in Week 6 short. picks.headline: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why?
picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs Missouri Predictions: Who Wins Critical Matchup and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Somewhat quietly, one of the bigger games on college football slate this weekend is happening at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium between No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) and No. 13 Missouri (5-1, 2-1 SEC). Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Sep 26, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on after an interception against the Florida Gators during the second half at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. He is a Biletnikoff Award and Lombardi Award voter from New Jersey with more than five years of sports reporting experience. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. Significant implications for the College Football Playoff. Over to Oxford, where either Mizzou or Ole Miss will finish Week 7 in a strong position to make a run in the second half of the 2026 regular season. No. 13-ranked Missouri football will face No. 10/9 Mississippi on Saturday, Oct. 17, in a Week 7 SEC matchup at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Mississippi. Like Eli Drinkwitz ended his midweek press conference, "look forward to seeing you on the SEC Network," with kickoff for the top-15 game set for 2:30 p.m. CT. The Tigers (5-1, 2-1 SEC) have won back-to-back league games over Florida and Texas A&M by multiple touchdowns. Mizzou's only loss so far this year was against the other half of the Egg Bowl, dropping a one-score game to Mississippi State in Starkville. Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1) bounced back from a loss to Florida with a blowout win over Vanderbilt this past Saturday in Nashville, Tennessee. Here's what Mizzou fans need to know about the Rebels, from their starting quarterback to their top playmakers, as well as a score prediction for the Week 7 game: Mizzou has 3 players from Ole Miss CFP roster, including QB Austin Simmons Anyone with a passing interest is aware: Austin Simmons is among three MU players going back to face their former team, along with wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. Simmons' situation is a little different. He's going to duke it out against the quarterback who took his starting job last season. Trinidad Chambliss was one of the stories of the season in 2025, leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff semifinals in his first season after transferring up from Division-II Ferris State. But the thing with Cinderella tales in sports … someone has to lose. That was Simmons, who began last year as the Rebels' starter. He's been widely praised in Oxford for how he handled the change and, essentially, a benching. He sustained an ankle injury in Week 2 and never got his job back. All's well that ends well. Simmons has found new life as the starter at Missouri and is beginning to generate some first-round NFL Draft interest. Chambliss is back in college because of an offseason court case that revolved around a medical redshirt during his time at Ferris State. Mizzou has a tough job defending Chambliss, who is currently fourth in the betting odds for the Heisman Trophy. He's mobile, has a tremendous arm and doesn't take too many sacks. Missouri has a dangerous offense, too, with Simmons and Lee leading the group. The winner is rewarded with a clearer path to making the CFP this year. "I wish them a lot of luck," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said Oct. 12, "other than this week when we're playing against them." More: Missouri football's biggest test yet comes in star Trinidad Chambliss More: Why Eli Drinkwitz isn't concerned with Ole Miss' familiarity with Austin Simmons How much does Kewan Lacy elevate Ole Miss offense? Speaking of reunions … Kewan Lacy started his career at Mizzou in 2024. He was a reserve behind Nate Noel and Marcus Carroll. He transferred to Ole Miss after his rookie year, which — talk about sliding doors moments — was among the reasons the Tigers added Ahmad Hardy out of the portal. Hardy and Lacy were Nos. 1 and 2 in the SEC for rushing yards last year, respectively, so the move worked out just fine for all parties. It'll be Lacy vs. Jamal Roberts on Saturday out of the backfield. Roberts currently leads the Power-conferences with 828 rushing yards. Lacy has been dealing with a shoulder injury and missed much of the start of this season. He returned this past Saturday in Ole Miss's win at Vandy with seven carries for 39 yards and a touchdown. Ole Miss's running numbers on the box score are modest, but the analytics paint a much prettier picture. The Rebels' rushing success rate of 60.7% ranks 10th nationally, per Hudl IQ. Every time they run the ball, they're generating 0.16 in 'Expected Points Added,' which is in the top five in the SEC (Missouri's EPA per rush is 0.05). A fully healthy Lacy can only help that cause. He forced 89 missed tackles last season, a number only bested by Hardy. He led the nation with 24 touchdowns. Sep 19, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels running back Kewan Lacy (5) carries the ball against the Louisiana State Tigers during the first quarter at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Ole Miss run defense has struggled So, Ole Miss's offense looks pretty good. The defense, however … The Rebels are allowing 392.4 yards per game, which is the second-most in the SEC. The kicker — Ole Miss is giving up 176.4 yards per game on the ground. That's the worst in the conference by quite some distance. Opponents' rushing success rate against Ole Miss is above 50%, per Hudl IQ, which means offenses are staying on schedule with more than half of their rushing attempts against the Rebels. Only Florida, which Mizzou gashed for 220 yards on the ground, Arkansas and Vanderbilt have defended the run worse in the SEC. Teams are generating runs of 15 or more yards 5.6% of the time against Ole Miss and runs of 30 or more yards 3.1% of the time. The Rebels have given up explosives. Roberts just became the third running back in the SEC in the last 20 years to run for 200 or more yards in back-to-back FBS games. The Tigers are committed to the run game, and unless Ole Miss has found a week-to-week fix, they should find some opportunities for Roberts to get loose. Missouri Tigers running back Jamal Roberts (20) celebrates with offensive lineman Tristan Wilson (73) after scoring against the Texas A&M Aggies during the second half of the game at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium on Oct. 10, 2026. Score prediction: Missouri 41, Ole Miss 38 When I wrote a game-by-game prediction on Aug. 29 before the season, I wrote the following about Mizzou's trip to Ole Miss: "Something about this game just feels like it's going to get weird. Break containment." I have not moved off of that prediction. My chaos radar is going berserk. I am, however, changing who I think will win. Ole Miss does not seem particularly adept at stopping the run. Roberts is not the back you want to see when you're struggling to contain chunk plays. The outside zone and fist fight it creates is not the scheme you want to work out the problems against. Mizzou's defense has been tremendous, but Ole Miss is going to score. The Rebels are too good not to. Our pregame prediction just has Missouri scoring more. away.blurb: Missouri football injury report Texas A&M: Tigers make 11 players available - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Missouri football injury report Texas A&M: Tigers make 11 players available Eleven of the 16 players who were on Missouri football's pregame availability reports between Wednesday and Friday were removed from the final pregame report, meaning all players who were not previously ruled out are available to play against Texas A&M. Mizzou had 16 players listed with five players listed as "out," seven players listed as "questionable" and four players listed as "probable." Now, the Tigers only have five players on the report, each of whom were already ruled out of playing against the Aggies. That means all of the following players should be able to play against Texas A&M: starting left tackle Cayden Green, starting defensive ends Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith, starting linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr., starting safeties Santana Banner and Kensley Louidor-Faustin, return specialist/wide receiver DaMarion Fowlkes, starting tight end Brett Norfleet, rotational cornerback Jahlil Florence, rotational defensive end Jaden Jones and backup linebacker Bobby Washington. The five players who were ruled out are running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, backup safety JaDon Blair, reserve tight end Gavin Hoffman and right tackle Josh Atkins. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable/game-time decision; doubtful; out. Texas A&M (3-2, 1-2) listed three players on its final report. Most notably, starting wide receiver Mario Craver is listed as a "game-time decision." Offensive lineman Blake Ivy and wideout Terry Bussey have been ruled out. Two players have been downgraded to "doubtful" to play: starting tight end Brett Norfleet and rotational linebacker Jeremiah Beasley. Two players are "questionable" to play: starting defensive lineman Sterling Webb and starting linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. Seven players are listed as "probable" to play: Starting QB Austin Simmons, starting left tackle Cayden Green, starting wide receiver Cayden Lee, key edge rushers Darris Smith and Daeden Hopkins, starting safety Santana Banner and backup corner Cam Keys. Mizzou, as expected, ruled out running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, right tackle Josh Atkins, reserve safety JaDon Blair and backup tight end Gavin Hoffman for this weekend's game. The Tigers also downgraded backup right guard Khalief Canty Jr., who is now officially ruled out of playing Ole Miss. Before a 27-6 win over Texas A&M this past Saturday, Mizzou listed 16 players on its midweek availability reports. As usual, the game has ACC and national title race implications , though this season those conversations are focused far more on Miami, which finished last season as the national runner-up and is currently the heavy favorite to win the ACC in 2026. Things are far different for Florida State and embattled coach Mike Norvell, who entered the year facing serious job pressure and now risks falling to 3-4 on the season and 1-3 in ACC play if the Seminoles cannot pull a stunning upset. Wins against Miami in 2021, 2022 and 2023 were crucial building blocks of Norvell's eventual ACC Championship run, but now it's Mario Cristobal who has the chance to string together three straight wins in the series after the Hurricanes got the better of Florida State in 2024 and 2025. The return to Miami Gardens also spotlights what has become a notable home-field advantage for Miami in this recent run, as the Hurricanes are 15-1 at home since the start of the 2024 season, including that 36-14 win against the Seminoles in Hard Rock Stadium two years ago. Miami has been absolute rock stars in the ACC and the sport as a whole, continuing the momentum from the team's College Football Playoff run with eye-popping scores and stat-stuffing performances to start the 2026 season. Florida State hopes to provide more resistance than the average Miami opponent, but even that might not be enough to stop the ACC's most potent national title contender. Miami vs. Florida State: Need to know A big stage for Darian Mensah's Heisman Trophy case: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been playing at an elite level all season, but the lopsided wins and predicted blowouts haven't given him the stage and audience that Saturday night's rivalry game will command. Miami may be in a far better place than Florida State this season, but this iconic rivalry will still bring the attention of Heisman Trophy voters to Hard Rock Stadium to see how Mensah performs under the pressure. Currently, he's one of just two FBS quarterbacks with 15-plus passing touchdowns and zero interceptions and boasts the best completion percentage (84.2%) and passer rating (212.2) in all of FBS. Mensah will still have a road trip to Notre Dame and a few other opportunities to shine in the spotlight, but Saturday night could prove to be the launching point for Mensah to push Jeremiah Smith in the Heisman conversation. Florida State struggling against top teams : While Florida State has won three national championships and spent 72 weeks ranked No. 1 in the AP Top 25 poll throughout its history, the Seminoles have struggled against the best teams in recent years. As the Seminoles take aim at their rival from the South, they do so staring down a brutal losing streak against top-3 teams from the AP poll. Florida State has lost its last eight games against AP top-three teams, last winning in the BCS National Championship Game against Auburn at the end of the 2013 season. Another losing streak that Florida State can put to bed on Saturday night is a 12-game road losing streak against teams with any AP ranking, which stretches back to a 2016 win at Miami. No one is beating teams like Miami is in 2026 : The Hurricanes enter this annual rivalry checkpoint with one of the most dominant teams in the country, beating opponents by an average of 39.8 points per game. That's the largest points-per-game differential through five games in school history and is currently the largest among all FBS teams. Now, a skeptic would be quick to point out that a 70-point win against Florida A&M will do a lot to juice those averages, but it's the consistency with which Miami has been blitzing its opponents that stands out. Of Miami's five games, only one (a 33-20 win at Wake Forest ) was decided by less than 28 points. Where to watch Miami vs. Florida State live Date : Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time : 7 p.m. ET Location : Hard Rock Stadium -- Miami Gardens, Fla. TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Miami vs. Florida State prediction, picks Miami isn't just blowing teams out on the scoreboard this season; it's a team that's also been exceeding oddsmakers' expectations nearly every week. The Hurricanes indeed have the best point differential in FBS (+39.8), but they also rank T-14 nationally with a 4-1 record against the spread and carry the 15th-best cover margin in the country, beating the spread by an average of 7.8 points per game. With those kinds of trends, it's tough to think that Miami is a candidate for an upset alert, and Florida State's road woes make it very possible that this game will get sideways on the Seminoles. Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. (Photo by Chris Leduc/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Cameron Underwood Fri, October 16, 2026 at 11:18 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Welcome back! In case you missed it, Saturday's rivalry game between the Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles is on deck, and we're here to share our predictions for the game. Call your shot. How does Canes vs Noles play out, who wins, and what's the score? Cam Underwood: Miami is clearly the superior team and superior program, and that's going to play out on the field. Miami is bigger, faster (save Danzy), stronger, and just flat out better than FSU. The spread opened with Miami as 3 touchdown favorites, and that's probably conservative to be honest. Miami wasn't even favored by this much when they beat FSU by 6 touchdowns in 2020. This should reasonably be a repeat of that kind of score line. This one won't be close, and I'm not going to let the colors of the jerseys sway me from that thought. This will be an epic asskicking and I'm going to enjoy every moment of it. Miami 55 Florida State 10 Justin Dottavio: THROW OUT THE RECORD BOOKS!!! As the Solid Verbal says. If I'm FSU and Mike Norvell I'm going to pull out every last stop. He likes trick plays, be aware of the onside kicks, fake punts, fake FG's, double reverse passes etc. Do I think that works? No. I think Miami should dominate the FSU I saw on tape from the Louisville game. But it is a rivalry game and it could have tricky aspects. Miami has been banged up but a bye week prior to the FSU game was a perfect placement. I think Miami wins this by 17+ and it could get ugly if the 'Noles quit. If I have to pick a final score it's Miami 45 FSU 20. Craig T. Smith: It's Miami and Florida State, and that always gives me pause about a blowout. Even the last two years, where Miami was light years better than FSU, there were moments where this game was closer than it should have been. And then, I went and checked the yardage that Florida State's defense has allowed this year. SMU, Alabama, and Louisville all went for well over 500 years each. Uh oh. Miami is the best offense and team that the Seminoles will face this year. Darian Mensah is on one right now, and Miami's offensive line has found its groove lately in run blocking. The Canes' defense also will have two starters back in Marquise Lightfoot and Xavier Lucas. This one is going to get ugly after all, folks. Miami 52, Florida State 23 Mike Schiffman: I am always fearful of a jinx. But not this year. I do think the 'Noles will come out swinging and have some success on a few scripted plays. Beyond that, I don't see them doing much on offense, especially with Xavier Lucas returning to cover FSU wide receiver Duce Robinson. On the other side of the ball, Miami is too creative with too much talent. Mensah and Co. will get their points. If the weather is bad, that could slow down the scoring some, but not enough. Miami 38, Florida state 10 Jake Marcus: The injury bug has hovered over Miami all season, but the bye week came at exactly the right time (although this season will likely be themed "next man up"). Xavier Lucas, Damari Brown, Marquise Lightfoot, and Ezekiel Marcelin are expected back, and the Canes enter rivalry night as the nation's top scoring offense (49.6 PPG) and top scoring defense (9.8 PPG allowed) – that's pretty damn good. Florida State comes in 3-3 after a 44-20 loss at Louisville, where it gave up 397 rushing yards even after a promising start out of the gates. Duce Robinson is the one player on the Noles' side who can flip a game. The 6-foot-6 senior caught 1,081 yards last year and led the ACC in contested-catch rate, but he's been relatively quiet this fall (17 catches, 294 yards through six games). He's still the lone matchup problem, but he'll face a secondary that's finally closer to full strength. Rain and thunderstorms are very likely at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday night, which could mean a sloppy, turnover-prone game and might nudge FSU toward leaning on Ashton Daniels and its run game. While sometimes weather and rivalry aspects can play 'equalizer', the wet conditions only shrink the margin for the team with the thinner roster and that's not close here. I like Miami's front to win early, and Darian Mensah doesn't need perfect weather to build a first-half cushion. By the fourth quarter the Canes will be sending in the backups, and the calls for Mike Norvell's job will only get louder heading into FSU's bye. Miami 41, Florida State 6 . Rob Weaver: This Saturday night the Florida State Seminoles will quite literally subject themselves to a storm. Only once this season – a dimly lit affair to open the season – have the Seminoles not scored at least 34 points. FSU running back Ousmane Kromah is one of only two ACC backs to have rushed 100 times this season, and he's maintaining a very respectable 5.7 yds per carry. WR Duce Robinson is a preseason all-conference selection. The weapons are there for FSU. And yet, the Hurricanes' unequivocally best defense in the conference (just 249 yds and 9.8 pts allowed per game) are returning multiple contributors from injury. Darrian Mensah and crew will get theirs, but the hallmark of this game will be the Hurricanes defense outclassing FSU unlike Alabama, Louisville, or any other of FSU's opponents. Miami 38, Florida State 13 There you have it. Our predictions for Canes vs Seminoles. How do YOU see the game playing out? Hop in the comments and share your thoughts.

Miami enters the matchup undefeated at 5-0 overall and 3-0 in ACC play, while Florida State sits at 3-3 and 1-2 in conference action. The Hurricanes are coming off a bye week, while the Seminoles are looking to rebound from a 44-20 loss to Louisville. Kickoff is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. With Miami chasing a potential College Football Playoff appearance and Florida State searching for consistency, this rivalry game carries plenty of importance. Darian Mensah Leads Miami's Offense Miami quarterback Darian Mensah has been outstanding during the Hurricanes' undefeated start. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards and 15 touchdowns without an interception, giving head coach Mario Cristobal a highly efficient passing attack. His accuracy and ability to get the ball to Miami's playmakers have helped the Hurricanes become one of the nation's most productive offenses. Wide receiver Malachi Toney has emerged as a major weapon, while Miami's running game gives the offense another way to control games. Running backs Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory have combined for 596 rushing yards, helping Miami maintain a balanced attack. Cristobal's team has also been strong defensively, allowing fewer than 10 points per game in ACC competition. That balance has helped Miami establish itself as a serious contender for the conference title. Florida State Needs a Response Florida State enters the rivalry looking for answers after its disappointing loss at Louisville. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has been one of the Seminoles' most dangerous rushing threats, scoring 10 rushing touchdowns through six games. Running back Ousmane Kromah has also been productive, recording 565 rushing yards. Head coach Mike Norvell will need his offense to maintain that rushing production while limiting mistakes against Miami's defense. The Seminoles have shown they can compete with strong opponents, including an early season lead against Alabama, but they have struggled to finish games consistently. Defensively, Florida State must improve its run defense after allowing 397 rushing yards against Louisville. That weakness could be especially concerning against Miami's powerful backfield. A Rivalry With Major Stakes Miami has won the last two meetings between the programs and will look to extend that streak at home. The Hurricanes want to remain undefeated and strengthen their national championship hopes. Florida State needs a complete performance to get its season back on track. With Mensah leading Miami and Daniels providing a dual-threat presence for Florida State, the quarterback matchup will be a key storyline. Saturday night offers Miami another opportunity to make a statement, while Florida State faces a difficult test against its biggest rival.

picks.headline: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Miami (FL)
picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Florida State Seminoles vs. Miami (FL) | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation October 17, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football FSU looks to avoid 14th straight loss in games away from Doak The Florida State Seminoles (3-3, 1-2) are in North Dade for their annual rivalry game against the 3rd-ranked Miami (FL) Hurricanes at Hard Rock Stadium on Saturday. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:00 p.m., and ESPN will televise the game. Miami (5-0, 3-0) leads the all-time series 37-33, while FSU holds a 21-19 edge in games played at Miami. The Seminoles are 13-9 in the series since Miami joined the ACC before the 2004 season but have lost the last two games, including a 28-22 loss last season in Tallahassee. FSU’s last victory over UM came in 2023, a 27-20 win at Doak, marking the Noles third win in a row against Miami (FL). UM’s Mario Cristobal is in his 5th season and has a 40-19 record in Miami and a 102-79 overall career record as a head coach. Miami opened its 2026 ACC slate with three straight road game wins over Stanford, Wake Forest, and Clemson and is one of only three teams with three Power-4 road wins. Miami is coming off a bye week after a 41-13 win over Clemson on the road last time out on Oct. 3. UM, led by mercenary QB Darian Mensah, who was purchased away from Duke via the transfer portal, has thrown 15 touchdowns with no interceptions. Mark Fletcher Jr. is their rushing leader, averaging 76.75 yards per game with 5 touchdowns, followed by freshman Javian Mallory, who averages 57.8 yards per game and has scored 3 TD’s. Receiver Malachi Toney, a name Seminole fans will get tired of hearing, is Mensah’s favorite target, catching 39 passes with a 15.49 average and 6 touchdowns. Cooper Barkate, who was part of the Mensah portal purchase package from Duke, is 2nd on the team with 19 receptions with a 12.68 average per game and 4 touchdowns. Overall, 14 players have caught passes from UM quarterbacks this season, 21 different players have gained 10-or-more scrimmage yards, and 11 different players have 100+ scrimmage yards this year. Miami’s defense is ranked 1st in points allowed (9.8), 1st against the run (42.6), 5th in total defense (249.6), 69th against the pass, T-25th in red zone defense, and 8th in sacks per game. Former FSU kicker Jake Weinberg is perfect in his 5 field goal attempts. Florida State will try to avoid its 14th straight loss in games away from Doak after coming off an embarrassing performance at Louisville, when after jumping out to a 14-0 lead, the Cardinals outscored FSU 44-6 the rest of the way to their 44-20 win. Louisville 44, FSU 20: Seminoles blow early lead in latest embarrassing loss Florida State’s offense is ranked 56th in the nation in total offense, 62nd in scoring, 43rd in rushing, 80th in passing, and 73rd in red-zone offense. After giving up three touchdown runs of 40-plus yards (97, 44, 68) and allowing Louisville to rack up 537 total yards, FSU’s defense now ranks 122nd in the nation, giving up 410 yards/game, 114th in passing defense (244 yards/game), 100th in third-down percentage allowing opponents to convert 41% of the time on third-down attempts, and T-120th in first-down defense allowing their opponents 129 first downs this season. Florida State is currently trending as a 21.5-point underdog, with the over/under set at 56.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Miami Hurricanes Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. Jordan Silversmith (season record: 5-1) Not sure how much needs to be written here. The Hurricanes have a positional advantage at every spot, better coordinators than FSU, and are coming off a bye while playing at home. If being a 21-point underdog doesn’t explain the differences between the two teams, nothing will. We can talk about why there’s such a difference another day, but for Saturday, UM wins and covers. UM 45, FSU 17 Jessi Wynn (season record: 3-1) Although we’ve really seen Ashton Daniels come into his own and emerge as a leader on offense, I’m not sure it’ll be enough to take down the undefeated 5-0 Hurricanes. FSU showed a ton of potential during its two-game winning streak, but last week’s tough loss to Louisville was a setback. With Miami playing as well as it has, I just don’t think I can put my neck on the line for the Seminoles this week. Miami 35 , Noles 24 NoleThruandThru (season record: 6-0) I’m just here so I don’t get fined, especially this week. Like Ludacris says, Mario fills cups like Double Ds. Miami 62, FSU 20 Jon Marchant (season record: 5-1 ) The Hurricanes certainly look like a national title contender, though we may not know for certain until the playoffs. Miami might face only one top 25 team this regular season, and it’s not Florida State. Miami is much more talented, and whatever issues Mario Cristobal may or may not still have regarding game management it’s likely equalized by Mike Norvell’s own problems in that area. Is this Norvell’s last game? We’ll have to see. If he’s still the coach next Saturday I think the decision to retain him is being made after an embarrassing loss to a rival. Miami 52 , FSU 16 Tim Scribble (season record: 5-1) Miami should be able to name their score in this one. I expect Mario and crew to embarrass Florida State. Miami 50+, FSU 17 Matt Minnick (Season record: 4-2; ATS: 4-2) I felt so good about my pick to win last week after the first quarter. Wow, what an unmitigated disaster. Once again Mike Norvell’s program shows it is unable to take a punch, pick itself off the mat, and punch back. Strange things can happen in rivalry games right? Just look at OU shocking Texas last week in the Red River Rivalry. Maybe FSU can pull off a similar stu—haha, who am I kidding? I can’t even type the sentence without smirking. FSU’s secondary couldn’t cover a twin mattress with a king sheet. Now it must stop Mensah, Toney, and company? Come on. Mario Cristobal can smell blood in the water and he’s primed to attack. Miami leads by 20+ at the half and cruises. Miami 48, FSU 14 Jacob Smith (season record: 3-2 ) FSU is so cooked. That is all that needs to be said. Darian Mensah is playing like a Heisman-level quarterback. He hasn’t thrown a single interception this year. Everything about Miami says absurd in terms of their quality of play. Now, they haven’t played *anyone* worth being No. 3, but they have convincingly won against bad teams. Doesn’t matter. FSU is getting clobbered. Miami 67, FSU 3 LastNoleOfKrypton (season record: 4-1) Mario’s propensity to blow one isn’t going to stop this bloodbath. Miami 52 , FSU 17 Frank DNole (season record: 3-3) I am a broken FSU fan. However, while SCum is heavily favored, this game is actually a win-win for FSU. If FSU wins by playing its best road game since November 25, 2023, as 21-point dogs, at the rented stadium, against one of the top teams in the country in terms of buying transfer players in hopes of becoming relevant again after 25 years of mediocrity under 5 different head coaches, each of whom proclaimed they would bring back the u (Coker, Shannon, Golden, Richt, Diaz, and Cristoball), that would be cool. If that were to happen, it would be the biggest humiliation the Noles could give scum since the 47-0 thrashing in 1997 and could possibly cost them heavily in the polls and later in possible playoff consideration. #winning If FSU loses, especially if blown out, the Noles still win, in that it will speed up what needs to be done to move FSU along on making the needed changes on Sunday morning. SCum thinks they will be putting the final nail in Norvell’s tenure, and while that may be true, they are doing the Noles a favor by possibly forcing the administration to act sooner than they may have wanted to. If that happens and the delusional scummers think it happened because they beat FSU, bless their hearts, all it will do is help speed up what was going to happen anyway and what most Noles want. So thanks? #winning Here is how I’m going to look at this game: Florida State is the last program to win a national championship in the state of Florida. FSU has won 5 ACC titles since scum joined the self-proclaimed All Canes Conference in 2004, and they still have zero titles 21 years later. Kudos to them for buying their way into the playoffs last year, but until you win an ACC title or a National Championship, a win tonight would just be another meaningless regular-season win. If scum, with the amount of money they have invested in their star-studded roster, do not win the National Championship, or at the very least the ACC championship this year, they never will. Finally, as a broken Seminole fan, I will watch this game with zero expectations, comfortably numb (shout to TN member ?), with the TV on mute and listening to Rage Against The Machine being played backwards. That said, FSU players… blah blah 110% more effort, blah… want it more, and blah blah… more heart than their more talented and better coached opponent. FSU Seminoles 37, FMFFM 34 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 3-3, 3-3 ATS) In 2024, we saw Mario Cristobal play it relatively safe instead of attempting to set a new record for margin of victory (47) in the series, with Miami winning by “just” 22. I don’t think that happens this year, a season where the Hurricanes are trying to make up for their lack of a difficult schedule with blowouts on top of trying to pad stats for Darian Mensah’s finish-in-second Heisman campaign. Florida State won’t be shut out, Ousmane Kromah should have at least a few exciting runs and maybe another cool Micahi Danzy catch. Outside of that, though, barring a hilarious meltdown from Miami, that should be just about the extent of positive takeaways from the matchup. away.headline: Initial week 7 injury report for Florida State vs. No. 3 Miami could spell disaster for the Seminoles
away.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. The Seminoles cannot win this game if quarterback Darian Mensah is given a clean pock

away.blurb: Lightfoot suffered an undisclosed injury in the first half of Miami's win against Clemson on Oct. 3 . Matt McCoy came out of the Clemson game with an injury before returning and finishing the game. Cristobal said McCoy was set to play against FSU this weekend. home.blurb: Florida State needs some luck on its side to take down Miami, but that might not happen with multiple players notably absent from the initial injury report . The Hurricanes had two starters in particular suffer injuries last time out against Clemson, but neither player was included in the injury report, which means the Seminoles will be getting the best version of Miami in Week 7. DB Romanas Frederique Jr. (out) LB Noah LaVallee (questionable) No Lightfoot and no McCoy on the injury report likely means Florida State will be playing against a full-strength Miami team. The Hurricanes have a few players who have been ruled out for the game, but nothing serious has changed from last week. That could be an issue for the Seminoles, who already will face two serious mismatches in Week 7. The Hurricanes' offense could also receive a boost if McCoy avoids having to sit out the Week 7 game against the Seminoles. There is no two ways about it, Florida State has struggled to generate consistent pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season. The performance against Virginia in Week 5 was exceptional, but it should be viewed as the outlier at this point, with more disappointing performances than positive ones on defense. Florida State is just days away from perhaps the biggest game on the schedule against ACC rivals No. 3 Miami. The Hurricanes have displayed arguably the best offense and the best defense in the country this season, while the Seminoles have struggled to play consistent football. Starting edge rusher and Miami's sack leader, Marquise Lightfoot, left the game against Clemson early, but the star defender was not included in the first Week 7 injury report. Additionally, starting right tackle Matthew McCoy was attended to by the training staff against the Tigers, but ultimately played the rest of the game. McCoy was also not included in the initial Week 7 injury report for Miami. Marquise Lightfoot, Matthew McCoy left off Miami's initial injury report for the Florida State game For Miami, getting Lightfoot back would be tremendous due to how quickly he can create an impact on the field. Lightfoot disrupts offenses, and Florida State's best chance at igniting the offense is by giving the football to dynamic running back Ousmane Kromah. The running back has been the one constant this season for the Seminoles' offense, but he may meet his match against Lightfoot. Lightfoot currently has 20 total tackles and five sacks this season, with a sack in each of his last four games. The defender also recorded a sack and two tackles against Clemson before exiting, and while Miami has a lot of talent capable of filling the potential void, nobody creates quite as much chaos as Lightfoot does. It is going to be very hard for Florida State, a team that already struggles with generating pressure, to do so against a team like Miami, who have only allowed five total sacks this season. LSU might have the best mix of talent, and it certainly has the highest-profile head coach, but it has two losses, and one of them was last week in a 35-34 overtime thriller to Kentucky. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Start here – it's just not screwing up. UK turned it over three times in the loss to Alabama, twice in a win over South Alabama, and that's it. No turnovers on the road at Texas A&M and South Carolina, and none last week against LSU. And then there are the penalties – there aren't any. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. And … Kentucky vs Oklahoma Prediction, Betting Lines Kentucky's only loss came in the one game (Alabama) it failed to hit 100 yards rushing and didn't score a touchdown on the ground. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 17, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. picks.headline: How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas).
