away.headline: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma Injury Report: Updates on CJ Baxter, Nic Anderson, and more
away.blurb: For Kentucky, the big news is that running back CJ Baxter is questionable to play this week. Baxter got dinged in the second half of the win over LSU but still finished the game and ran for a touchdown in overtime. He’s been one of the SEC’s best backs thus far, so not having him in Norman would be a major setback for this offense. Wide receiver Nic Anderson, who left last week’s win over LSU with a shoulder injury, is listed as probable, so he should be good to go this week as long as there are no setbacks. Defensive tackle Kalen Edwards, who missed last week, is questionable to play. As expected, linebacker Antwan Smith and cornerback Jaden Smith remain out after suffering injuries at South Carolina. Linebacker Tavion Wallace, out for the past two weeks, is still listed as out. Fellow linebacker Alex Afari Jr. is listed as questionable as he works through the legal process in hopes of regaining eligibility. He’s healthy, so if granted eligibility in the courts, he should play Saturday, but that’s a big if right now. Cornerback Grant Grayton remains out. Reserve defensive end Tyler Thomas is doubtful. home.headline: Oklahoma vs. Kentucky Injury Report: Sooners offensive line banged up
home.blurb: After initially being listed as questionable, Michael Fasusi and Heath Ozaeta, a pair of players who have started a number of games for the Sooners over the last two seasons, were downgraded to doubtful. They joined fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis as doubtful. This comes after Head coach Brent Venables said Fasusi was "just about ready" to make his return on Tuesday. Well, it looks like we'll have to wait another week for Fasusi's return. With Fasusi, Ozaeta, and Pierre-Louis doubtful for Saturday, the Sooners will have another combination starting up front for the Sooners. Ryan Fodje will continue to start at left tackle with true freshman Noah Best at left guard. Jake Miakkula will be at center once again with E'Marion Harris at right tackle. That leaves right guard as the question mark. Peyton Joseph is probably the player coming off the bench to start for the Sooners. He's been a rotational player at guard this season, playing 47 snaps this season. Starting cornerback Eli Bowen has been ruled out for Saturday, putting Trystan Haynes in line to make his second straight start. For the Kentucky Wildcats , one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. He remains questionable for Saturday, and Pete Nakos of On3 says he'll be a game-time decision. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). Fasusi has missed the last four games after playing with a shoulder injury against UTEP. Ozaeta was banged up in warm-ups ahead of the Red River Showdown, but still played 59 snaps up front. One of them will leave Autzen Stadium with what could be a damaging second conference loss of the season. Oregon is coming off a 17-15 upset defeat at the hands of then-No. 21 UCLA in which coach Dan Lanning’s Ducks squad turned the ball over seven times and was successful just once on 13 third-down conversions. With quarterback Dante Moore still out with a concussion, Oregon turns to a tandem of quarterbacks in Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Nebraska had then-No. 7 Indiana on the ropes last week, only to watch as Hoosiers wide receiver Nick Marsh victimized them for two long touchdowns and a late 20-17 win over the Cornhuskers at Memorial Stadium. Uncertainty Under Center Oct. 10, 2026; Eugene, Oregon; Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola scrambles versus the UCLA Bruins at Autzen Stadium. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect If going up against the nation’s No. 16 defense wasn’t a tall-enough task, Oregon must do so without Moore, who remains out while recovering from the injury suffered in Week 4 against USC. If going up against the nation’s No. 16 defense wasn’t a tall-enough task, Oregon must do so without Moore, who remains out while recovering from the injury suffered in Week 4 against USC. Raiola impressed in relief of Moore, guiding the Ducks past the Trojans, only to struggle mightily in his first start with Oregon, throwing for just 43 yards (6-of-19) and two interceptions. Thomas replaced the wildly inefficient Raiola in the fourth quarter and accounted for 156 of the team’s 272 total yards on the day. If Raiola gets the starting nod under center, he’ll be facing his former team in Nebraska, where he passed for 4,819 yards and 31 touchdowns. Whoever starts for Lanning’s squad will stare across the line at a Huskers’ defense that has simply been dominant. Nebraska is allowing just 15.2 points and 276.2 yards per game with the nation’s best third-down defense (19.7 percent), ahead of No. 2 Oregon (22.1 percent). The Ducks must support Raiola or Thomas with an established run game, something that’s been lacking in Oregon's offense, which has yet to produce a 100-yard rushing performance from either running backs Jordon Davison or Dierre Hill Jr. They’ll have to do so against a Nebraska rush defense that ranks No. 17 in the country versus the run at 94.7 yards per game. Yet the Ducks remain vulnerable against the pass (226.0 yards per game) and rank just No. 41 nationally against the run (118.4 yards per game). Yet the Ducks remain vulnerable against the pass (226.0 yards per game) and rank just No. 41 nationally against the run (118.4 yards per game). That could leave them exposed versus Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea, who has already racked up 1,405 passing yards, 296 yards on the ground and 16 total touchdowns. Oregon has experienced mixed results defending against mobile quarterbacks. The Ducks limited UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava to one net rushing yard before he exited at halftime with an expected season-ending knee injury, while surrendering 326 passing yards to quarterback Jayden Maiava in their win over USC. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! Stay up to date on all things Huskers by bookmarking Nebraska Cornhuskers On SI , following us on Twitter/X , and visiting HuskerMax.com daily. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. picks.blurb: Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Expert score prediction: Nebraska vs. Oregon Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Nebraska's loss to Indiana last week stung, with the team dropping a 17-6 lead to the defending national champion. Now the Huskers travel up to Oregon for a 10 p.m. CT matchup, the latest start time for Nebraska since 2014. But other factors in this game make this clash all the more questionable. Dante Moore is out for the game, meaning Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas or even Akili Smith Jr. will be earning the start. But Raiola is the most poetic option after all and is likely the starter despite a rough outing against UCLA. After going 19-of-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns against USC, Raiola only threw 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions against the Bruins . He also got strip-sacked in the game. Though it was Raiola's only sack, UCLA still brought the pressure throughout. Raiola's main weakness is pressure, which the Bruins exploited last week. Though Raiola can find ways to stay alive in the pocket and deliver big plays, he rarely takes off downfield and has found himself in rough spots. Thomas took over in the fourth quarter for the Ducks and went 11-of-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown. He did, however, fumble on his opening drive but nearly completed the comeback. But even if Thomas starts, it remains to be seen whether he can replicate that success, especially after seeing Raiola's two-game stretch. Now, Nebraska can get to the quarterback, but the concern comes down to the explosive plays. Indiana pulled off multiple explosive plays last week, despite its struggle to produce points and yardage for most of the game. The Ducks can do the same, especially late in the game. Nebraska ran out of steam in the fourth against Indiana at home early in the afternoon. Now, the Huskers face Oregon on the road after dark. The Ducks almost completed their 17-6 comeback against UCLA, so they can find a way to do the same against Nebraska if needed. The Huskers' defense also needs to be cautious with Oregon's rushing game. Though the Ducks don't strike primarily on the ground, Dierre Hill Jr. and Jordon Davison combined for 216 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 54 carries over the last two games, averaging four yards per carry. Though UCLA did suffocate Oregon's run at times, Nebraska could let a play slip by if it's not careful. Oregon's defense also needs to be cautious, seeing how its last two games panned out. The Ducks held USC to 27 points, but Jayden Maiava still threw for 326 yards and two touchdowns on just 23 completions. Oregon also surrendered 205 passing yards on just 13 completions to UCLA, despite holding it to 17 points. Nebraska could do some damage on the run, however. Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker tallied 109 rushing yards earlier this season against the Ducks. Anthony Colandrea could do the same and help the Huskers score. Jamal Rule, Mekhi Nelson and Isaiah Mozee all could have moments as well after UCLA's Wayne Knight found some holes in Oregon's defensive line. Knight finished with 103 yards on 22 carries. But this game is also make-or-break for Oregon's postseason hopes, especially with Ohio State and even Northwestern coming up. The Ducks also have a talented roster and, despite their issues, can deliver major blows to opponents when momentum is on their side. Nebraska's issues on the line, in the secondary and even a bit on special teams don't help either. All of this, plus the after-dark setting, provides just enough to tip the scales in the Ducks' favor. Unless Nebraska can truly come out and play like a team that can earn a top-25 spot, this matchup will likely be another so-close-but-so-far loss. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Greg Liodice Sat, October 17, 2026 at 10:30 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nebraska Cornhuskers take on the Oregon Ducks in Eugene, OR. Kickoff is set for 11 p.m. ET on FOX. Oregon is favored by -6.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -245. The total is set at 51.5 points. Here's my Nebraska vs. Oregon prediction and college football pick for Saturday, October 17, 2026. Nebraska vs. Oregon Pick: Nebraska +6.5 My Oregon vs. Nebraska best bet is on the Cornhuskers to cover. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Nebraska vs Oregon Odds Nebraska vs Oregon point spread : Oregon -6.5 (-118), Nebraska +6.5 (-104) Nebraska vs Oregon over/under : 51.5 (-110o / -110u) Nebraska vs Oregon moneyline : Nebraska +198, Oregon -245 One of the biggest storylines about the Nebraska season is how much better it got after Dylan Raiola left town. Anthony Colandrea has been a revelation since coming in from UNLV , completing 64% of his passes with an impressive 13:3 touchdown -to-interception ratio. Half of those passing scores went to Kwazi Gilmer, the UCLA transfer. Colandrea had a rough outing against Indiana , and for the most part, it seemed as if Nebraska was going to pull away. But in traditional Nebraska fashion, it ended up blowing it against the defending champs, losing 20-17. It was a rough outing for the Huskers' defense, a defense that has been really strong all season long. But Indiana scored on a one-play, 75-yard touchdown to Nick Marsh, which all but sealed the game for the Huskers. After that, the Hoosiers pulled away for good. Head coach Matt Rhule has developed a reputation at the college level that he can't win the big one. Last week proved that it's still true. The Huskers' run game should be used effectively, ranking 39th in Success Rate and third in explosiveness . Jamal Rule and Mekhi Nelson have split the carries, with Rule averaging 6.8 yards per carry and Nelson being more of a threat through the air. There's definitely a lot of talent on this defense, but they are prone to giving up big plays. Defensive back Dwayne McDougle has been a tackling machine and recorded an 81-yard pick-six. Nebraska's pass rush has also been really strong, generating Havoc on 18.5% of plays. DL Jahsear Whittington leads the team with 2.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Oregon has been one of the biggest disappointments this season. Coming into the season with championship hopes, it has now dropped two games in the first five games. The Ducks will continue to be without quarterback Dante Moore , and it may be Raiola getting the start against his old program, Nebraska. Raiola looked strong in relief against USC , completing 76% of his passes with a pair of touchdowns. However, when Oregon took on UCLA, Raiola was completely exposed, throwing two picks and only completing six out of 19 attempts. Ultimately, he was benched for Brock Thomas, a walk-on. It will hurt the Ducks this week, as they won't have wide receivers Jeremiah McClellan or Evan Stewart , which means Dakorien Moore will need to step up as more of a volume receiver. A big reason why this season has been brutal is because of Oregon's change of approach to the run. Last season, the Ducks averaged 36.6 rushing attempts per game, while this season, they average 28.8 attempts, which is 126th in the FBS. Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. have essentially split the carries, with Davison averaging just under five yards per carry. But they both have lacked the explosiveness needed to be truly effective. The run game may be ranked 62nd, but because Oregon doesn't run the ball as much, the offense has become very predictable. There are a ton of stars on this defense, including safety Koi Perich, who leads the team in solo tackles and two picks, as well as defensive tackle Matayo Uiagalelei, with five sacks. Overall, the Ducks have an impressive secondary, but the defense has been the clear definition of mediocre, so it's hard to take it seriously. I never thought, when looking at the schedule, of taking the Huskers to cover, but here we are. Oregon has been brutal when it comes to the spread, while the Huskers are 5-1. I'm typically not a believer in moral victories, but I think there's something to be said about how Nebraska had the Hoosiers on their heels for most of last week. The Huskers are better than their reputation says; it's really about closing games, which they still can't do. Needless to say, with the spread being a full touchdown, I don't think it's out of the question to pick Nebraska to cover. Whether it's Raiola or Thomas starting, I think this will end up being a positive for the Husker defense. Pick: Nebraska +6.5

Game preview, prediction, betting line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Ryan Clarke Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:23 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) seek to recapture momentum in what has been a massively disappointing 2026 season so far, and they'll have no time to rest and regroup as confident Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) comes to town. The Cornhuskers are coming off a highly competitive effort in a loss to defending national champions Indiana, while the Ducks have a quarterback battle to work out with Dante Moore still sidelined as he recovers from a concussion. Here is a preview: Oregon (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) vs. Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) When: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 8 p.m. PT Where: Autzen Stadium Latest line: Oregon by 7 Radio: Oregon Sports Network Stream : You can watch this game live with Fubo (free trial), or with DIRECTV (free trial). If you are out of free trials, you can also watch this game with Sling (cheapest streaming plans that include live sports). Streaming broadcasts for this game will be available on these streaming services locally in Oregon and Washington, but may not be available outside of the Pacific Northwest, depending on your location. LOOKING FOR REVENGE? Dylan Raiola will have to earn the opportunity to face his former team in Nebraska. A two-year starter for the Cornhuskers, Raiola has faced external criticism for his decision to transfer to Oregon, but he maintains a strong relationship with Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and several of his former teammates. Raiola's performance against UCLA last week was one of the worst by an Oregon quarterback in recent memory: 6 of 19 passing, 43 yards and two interceptions. This, just two weeks after a highly effective outing in relief of the injured Moore against USC. Raiola was pulled in the fourth quarter against UCLA in favor of Brock Thomas, who almost led a Ducks comeback. Akili Smith Jr. was apparently part of the quarterback competition this week, too. While it is far from a guarantee that Raiola will lead the Oregon offense out onto the field against Nebraska, his personal motivation could be enough to sharpen his focus and help earn him the chance — and perhaps bounce back in a big way performance-wise to lead the Ducks to victory. GETTING A PUSH Whether Raiola or any of the Oregon quarterbacks succeeds depends heavily on the men up front. Oregon's offensive line was dreadful last week after getting a strong push to establish the run just two weeks prior against USC. If the Ducks can't find balance and give Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill a chance to break off big plays, it will be a long day for whoever is tossing the pigskin for the Ducks and staring down Nebraska's edge rushers. Especially with top Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart listed as doubtful as of Thursday evening. Dan Lanning admitted this week that Oregon is still working out who its best five offensive linemen are. For a program that came into the season with major questions at the position and an entire spring and fall camp to figure those things out, that is a very bad sign. A MOBILE THREAT Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea is a talented athlete who can make things happen with his legs. He will provide the biggest test yet for Oregon's front seven in containing a mobile quarterback, one they failed when facing Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker but largely passed against USC's Jayden Maiava. For all the bad that showed up in Oregon's befuddling, 17-15 loss to UCLA last week, the defense played well for the most part. Save for a deep pass on the first play of the game and Wayne Knight's touchdown run in the second quarter, the Ducks looked like the defensive line unit many expected them to be coming into the season. This Saturday, maintaining that level of play will start and end with keeping Colandrea in check. Forcing him into tough situations and not allowing him to improvise into big plays on the ground could be the difference. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. home.headline: Why isn’t Dante Moore playing for Oregon against UCLA? The Ducks QB’s injury status
home.blurb: Moore returned to practice this week, but he remains in concussion protocol and was officially listed as out on Oregon’s availability report. The Ducks are taking a cautious approach to his recovery, with no timetable announced for his return. Moore returned to practice on Monday, October 5 , following Oregon’s bye week. His return was an encouraging development, but it did not mean he was ready to play. Lanning said the Ducks would continue to prioritize what was best for Moore as he worked through the recovery process. Moore remained in concussion protocol and was ruled out for the UCLA game on the conference’s availability report released Wednesday. The quarterback must complete the necessary steps in the concussion protocol before he can return to game action. Oregon has not announced a target date for his comeback. With Moore unavailable, Dylan Raiola is set to make his first start for Oregon . The former Nebraska quarterback replaced Moore against USC and helped the Ducks secure the victory, completing 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns . “He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really, really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice, ” Lanning said. home.headline: What we're hearing on Oregon injuries ahead of Nebraska
home.blurb: However, it doesn't appear that things are going to get any easier, with the Nebraska Cornhuskers coming to town, and starting quarterback Dante Moore once again ruled out after the concussion he suffered in Week 4 against the USC Trojans . That will leave either Brock Thomas, Dylan Raiola, or Akili Smith Jr. under center with the start, and a big onus on the offense to show some improvement. While the Big Ten Availability report was released on Wednesday and will again come out on Thursday and Friday nights, we've got some intel on where things stand with each injured player and whether or not they will be able to contribute this weekend. Here's our early look at who we think could potentially be out or limited in this game on Friday night. There was some hope that Dante Moore might be able to give it a go this week after returning to practice following his concussion, but the fact that he was ruled "out" in the first availability report, and not even "questionable," is not a great sign for an expedient return. We will see if Moore is able to go next week against Illinois, but it could still be a couple of weeks before we see No. 5 back on the field, if at all. McClellan has been out for a few weeks now after suffering a broken foot in warmups before the Portland State game, and has been seen wearing a walking boot during games. We will see when he is able to get out of the boot and back to practice, but it might still be several weeks, at the least. "He's going to be done for the foreseeable future. (It's) something he tried to tough out. You know, credit to him. Sometimes you can play through that, but you're probably not going to play as well. But it's one of those ones where it made sense to get it repaired for him." According to head coach Dan Lanning, Platt is still dealing with an undisclosed injury that held him out of the spring game earlier this year. Oregon's coach does not expect him to return to the field anytime soon. "He's gonna be limited for a while with the injury he felt in the spring," Lanning said of Platt. "I don't want to put a timeline on it, but he's going to be out for some time until we see where he's at and continue to progress and challenge himself." After suffering a neck injury during fall camp a year ago, Gresham was held out for the entire 2025 season and has yet to return to the field. Oregon still has him on the roster, but it doesn't sound like he will be back anytime soon. Colorado transfer RB Simeon Price is yet to play this year and has been seen in street clothes wearing a walking boot recently during Oregon games.
